cards.text: Some time later, the king of the Ammonites dies, and his son Hanun takes over as king. Over in Israel, King David hears about it. And he starts thinking about Hanun's father, Nahash.

cards.question: David says he'll show ___ to Hanun son of Nahash, just like Hanun's father showed him.
So David sends some of his servants to the new king Hanun. What are they there to do?

cards.text: David's servants arrive in the land of the Ammonites. And Hanun's princes? Oh, they've got THOUGHTS.

cards.question: What do Hanun's princes say David's servants are really there to do?

answers.text: Spy out the city and overthrow it
Take Hanun back as a prisoner

cards.text: Hanun goes along with his princes. Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and nobody EVER did me like what's coming next.

cards.question: What does Hanun do to the beards of David's servants?

answers.text: Shaves off half of each beard

cards.question: Hanun also cuts off the servants' garments at the hips before sending them away.

cards.text: Half a beard, half an outfit, and then Hanun sends them away. If somebody shaved off half MY mustache, friend, I'd be packing cookie boxes one-handed.
Word gets back to David. He sends messengers to meet his men, because they've been thoroughly humiliated.

cards.question: David has a message for his humiliated servants. When should they come home?
Until their beards grow back, David tells his servants to stay in ___.

cards.text: Take your time, fellas, let it grow out. It's like dodging the group chat after a bad haircut, except these guys didn't even pick the haircut.
Back in Ammon, the Ammonites realize they've become a stench to David.

cards.question: Once they realize they've become a stench to David, the Ammonites send him a gift to make peace.

cards.text: They hire twenty thousand Aramean foot soldiers from Beth-rehob and Zoba, a thousand men from the king of Maacah and twelve thousand from Tob. That's not a few extra hands, friend, that's a STADIUM.

cards.question: When David hears the Ammonites have hired all those soldiers, what does he do?

answers.text: Sends Joab his commander with the entire army
Sends his servants back to make peace with Hanun
Goes alone to talk things over with Hanun

cards.text: The Ammonites line up for battle at the entrance of their city gate. Their hired soldiers, the Arameans and the men of Tob and Maacah, set up by themselves out in the open country.
Joab, leading David's army, sees battle lines in front of him AND behind him. Friend, that's a semi truck in front of you and another one riding your bumper.

cards.question: Joab has enemies in front of him and behind him. What does he do with Israel's army?
Joab picks some of the ___ men of Israel and lines them up against the Arameans.

cards.text: The rest of the troops go to Joab's brother, Abishai, who lines them up against the Ammonites. Then Joab gives his brother a plan.

cards.question: What plan does Joab give his brother Abishai before the battle?

answers.text: If one of them is overpowered the other comes to help
If one of them wins first he chases the enemy home
If one of them is overpowered they both retreat

cards.text: That's two coworkers saying, "If your line gets slammed, I'll jump on it. If mine does, you jump on mine." Same deal, just a MUCH bigger shift.

cards.question: Joab tells Abishai to be strong and fight bravely. Who does he say they're fighting for?

answers.text: Their people and the cities of their God
King David and the honor of his name
The servants Hanun sent home humiliated

cards.text: Then Joab says, "May the LORD do what is good in His sight." Fight hard, then leave it with the LORD. That's the whole plan.

cards.question: When Joab and his troops advance, the Arameans hold their ground and fight.

cards.text: The Ammonites see the Arameans run, so they run too, right back into their city, and Joab heads home to Jerusalem. All that hiring, and the hired help clocked out early.
The Arameans see they've been defeated by Israel, so they regroup. Hadadezer, king of Zobah, sends messengers to bring more Arameans from beyond the Euphrates.

cards.question: The new Aramean troops gather at Helam. Who is leading them?

answers.text: Shobach the commander of Hadadezer's army
Hanun the king of the Ammonites
Hadadezer himself at the very front

cards.question: When David hears about the Arameans at Helam, he stays in Jerusalem and sends Joab out again.

cards.text: This time the king comes himself. David gathers all Israel, crosses the Jordan and goes to Helam, and the Arameans line up and fight him.

cards.question: The Arameans fight David at Helam. How does it go for them?

answers.text: They push Israel back across the Jordan

cards.text: David strikes down seven hundred charioteers and forty THOUSAND foot soldiers. Friend, I lose count stamping a dozen cookies.

cards.question: What happens to Shobach, the commander of the Aramean army?

answers.text: He is struck down and dies there
He escapes back beyond the Euphrates
He is taken to Jerusalem as a prisoner

cards.question: The kings who answered to Hadadezer see they've been defeated by Israel. What do they do?

answers.text: Make peace and become subject to Israel
Hire another army from Tob and Maacah
Hide inside the Ammonite city with Hanun

cards.question: After all this, the Arameans are still ready to help the Ammonites.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats what the baker already has. Card 7 covered the half beards, and card 8 covered the garments cut at the hips and being sent away. The card adds no new moment from the passage and exists to carry the mustache joke.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: This is a recap card. 'Half a beard, half an outfit, and then Hanun sends them away' restates the answers to cards 7 and 8.
This story card tells no new part of the passage. 'Take your time, fellas, let it grow out' restates the answers to cards 11 and 12. The rest of the card is only the group chat joke.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: This story card only restates Joab's plan, which the baker just answered on card 6. It moves the passage nowhere and is only the coworker joke.

findings.problem: The right answer calls Joab 'his commander.' That fact comes from outside the passage (2 Samuel 8:16), but the card cites only 2 Samuel 10:7 and gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card calls Hadadezer 'king of Zobah.' That fact comes from outside the passage (2 Samuel 8:3), but the card cites only 2 Samuel 10:15-16 and gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates stop 2 by a wide margin. Of the 11 choice cards, 7 are multiple choice, 3 are true or false and only 1 is fill in the blank. Cards 16, 18 and 19 are three multiple choice cards in a row.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
